newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods drops sale of retail division.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods drops sale of retail division.

text.p: British privately-owned retail-to-football pools company Littlewoods should see "positive signs" from its new strategy on its high street stores within three years, chairman James Ross told Reuters on Monday.

Littlewoods, which put the stores division up for sale in March, said in a statement it had decided to retain most of its retail outlets, refocus its store strategy and sell off selected properties, which had seen interest from buyers.
"To turn around you would need five years but I will be disappointed if there are no positive signs within three," Ross said, adding that the company expected to keep over 100 of its 135 stores.

It aimed to realise value by selling selected key properties, for which it had had "some very interesting offers," Ross said, but declined to specify potential buyers, saying that "we have not got to that process yet...(we'll be) entering that fairly soon."

Littlewoods would aim to focus on its Berketex higher quality brand, Ross said, targeting women shoppers over 45 years old, who buy for themselves and their partners, with shop sizes standardised to 10,000-15,000 square feet. It would sub-let, let or sell extra selling space in larger sites.

Littlewoods had struggled since March to find a buyer for all its stores, which carried a suggested price tag of 500 million pounds ($831.1 million), with pressure increasing from potential buyers for it to sell the outlets on a piecemeal basis. ($ = 0.601 British Pounds)
